title: api-gateway: tune streaming proxy buffers and routing rules to stabilize function-calls & structured output (OpenAI compat)
author: Ava Mitchell
release_notes: Adjusted streaming proxy buffer sizes and routing policies to improve stability for function calls and structured output in OpenAI-compat mode. Added safe fallbacks for truncated payloads and a feature-flagged rollout.
description:
Context: We observed increased streaming proxy OOMs and truncated structured outputs when large tool-calling payloads were routed through less-capable backends. This caused degraded user-facing behavior for OpenAI-compat endpoints (missing final tokens, aborted function calls) under bursty traffic. This PR tunes buffer sizing, strengthens routing predicates, and adds defensive fallbacks to reduce these failures while preserving latency SLOs.

What I changed (high level):
- Dynamic streaming proxy buffer regulator: introduce heuristics to grow/shrink per-connection buffers based on observed payload sizes and memory pressure.
- Routing rule tightening: prefer high-capacity serving pools for requests that include tool/function-calls or structured-output hints (Content-Type/structured-output header).
- Payload size limits and graceful truncation: clamp extremely large intermediate tool payloads at the proxy with a structured truncation marker so downstream callers and OpenAI-compat shim can handle incomplete tool-call payloads gracefully.
- OpenAI-compat shim: detect truncated streams and emit a final "truncated=true" metadata event so SDKs can surface an actionable error and the Console can link incidents.
- Feature flag + rollout: new flag api_gateway.streaming_buffer_regulator enabled=false by default for 2 days, then gradually rolled to 25/50/100% if no regressions.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests for regulator logic, [x] Integration test across small/medium/large model backends, [x] E2E test for function-calls with simulated bursty traffic, [x] Observability dashboards (buffers, truncations, routing decisions) added, [x] Feature flag + rollout plan.

Motivation and tradeoffs: Increasing buffers universally hides memory pressure and leads to capacity problems; regulator allows adaptive sizing with eviction heuristics. Tightening routing reduces tail failures but may slightly increase cost if more requests route to high-capacity pools - routing predicate is conservative (only for explicit tool/function hints). Truncation is a last-resort safety mechanism and is surfaced to clients to avoid silent data loss.

Related: ENG-2034 (streaming stability), PR #28142 and #39217 (historical API gateway streaming changes), SUP-4123 (customer incident), internal runbook link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2034/streaming-stability

Testing and rollout: see testing_notes and rollout_plan fields below for details.

testing_notes: Unit tests cover regulator behavior under simulated growth/shrink cycles and evictions. Integration runs validated end-to-end function-call streams with 50k messages across mixed backends; observed truncation events dropped from ~1.8% to <0.2% after regulator. Load test scripts are in integration/streaming_tests and were used to validate 25/50/100% rollout windows.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: 0% -> 2 days dry-run in canary -> 25% (48h) -> 50% (48h) -> 100% if no regressions. Observability alerts: >0.5% truncation rate or >20% increase in routing_to_high_capacity triggers automated rollback. Manual approval required to proceed beyond 50%.
notes_for_support: New truncated event 'truncated=true' will appear in stream termination metadata for affected requests. Support playbook: check 'truncation_count' metric, identify request id (X-Request-ID), and advise customers to retry with smaller tool payloads or request routing override via support. Linked incident SUP-4123 for workflow.
post_merge_actions: Remove feature flag gating after 2 weeks if stable; follow-up PR to enable by default and add cost monitoring. Announce in #platform-release and update API compatibility notes in redwood-docs.
